sources.title: Holomorphic Factorization at the Quantum Horizon

evidence.text: Separate the scalar equation and reduce its radial part to a hypergeometric horizon-skimming equation. Impose boundary normalizability and stretched-horizon Dirichlet conditions to obtain a Gamma-function phase equation, then approximate its low-lying solutions. The authors say other nondissipative wall conditions suffice for their claims.

sources.title: Microscopic origin of the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy

evidence.text: Reduce the wrapped-brane worldvolume theory to a two-dimensional supersymmetric sigma model, count right-moving-ground-state RR states through the elliptic genus, and apply the asymptotic oscillator formula d(n,c)∼exp(2π√(nc/6)). T-duality identifies the circle momentum P with Q_H.

sources.title: Black hole entropy from near horizon microstates

evidence.text: The paper reviews Brown–Henneaux boundary conditions, takes the quotient of allowed diffeomorphisms by those vanishing sufficiently rapidly at infinity, and imports the resulting pair of Virasoro algebras and central charge. BTZ parameters are then translated into left- and right-moving conformal levels.

sources.title: Holomorphic Factorization at the Quantum Horizon

evidence.text: Compute bosonic normal-mode partition functions separately for positive and negative azimuthal quantum numbers. Replace the radial sum by an integral, count angular degeneracies, and use inverse Laplace transformation with a saddle-point approximation to extract microcanonical entropy and Cardy-form expressions.

sources.title: Microscopic origin of the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy

evidence.text: Use the low-energy dilaton–gravity action with RR and axion field strengths, determine the constant-dilaton near-horizon solution from charge equations, and calculate its Einstein-frame S³ horizon area.

sources.title: Black hole entropy from near horizon microstates

evidence.text: Cardy’s asymptotic state-counting formula S=2π√(c nR/6)+2π√(c nL/6) is evaluated using c=3ℓ/(2G), nR+nL=ℓM, and nR−nL=J, and compared with the BTZ area entropy.

evidence.text: Solve a provisional species equation, test the next gap against its cutoff, and update the effective count whenever another tower is populated. Repeat in increasing gap order to determine the asymptotically relevant spectrum.

evidence.text: Compare species energy Esp=Σdnmn, count Nsp=Σdn, and microcanonical entropy with the black-hole scalings MBH∼Λsp^(3−d), SBH∼Λsp^(2−d), TBH∼Λsp. The count obeys Nsp=Λsp^(2−d) in Planck units.

evidence.text: Compare regularized Euclidean black-hole and Horowitz–Myers soliton actions, matching boundary periodicities. The soliton is obtained through double analytic continuation, and its parameters need not coincide with the black-hole parameters.

sources.title: Black string in the standard model

evidence.text: Solve the extremal boundary-value problem independently by shooting and modified gradient flow, with reported agreement. Integrate nonextremal solutions outward from a regular horizon, fit their vacuum asymptotics, and obtain temperature from Euclidean conical regularity.

sources.title: Bounding the Temperatures of Black Holes Dual to Strongly Coupled Field Theories on Flat Spacetime

evidence.text: Write the horizon equation as a cubic in x=r², select its larger positive root, and evaluate the large-radius brane action. The instability threshold follows when its positive horizon contribution ceases to offset the negative mass contribution.

evidence.text: Reduce the Einstein equations using radial metric ansätze and their first-order constraint. The extremal radial equation admits a mechanical interpretation with friction and an effective potential U; the nonextremal equations determine B and R before reconstructing A.
